description_full: Xenia Hotels & Resorts, Inc. is a self-advised and self-administered REIT that invests in uniquely positioned luxury and upper upscale hotels and resorts with a focus on the top 25 lodging markets as well as key leisure destinations in the United States. The Company owns 29 hotels and resorts comprising 8,783 rooms across 14 states. Xenia's hotels are in luxury and upper-scale segments and are operated and/or licensed by industry leaders including Marriott, Hyatt, Kimpton, Fairmont, Loews, Hilton, and Davidson. Xenia Hotels & Resorts, Inc. was incorporated in 2007 and is based in Orlando, United States.

financial_summary: Xenia Hotels & Resorts, Inc. is a mid-cap real estate business with a $2.1B market cap on $1.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +3% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 4% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $90M in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.80× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 5.4× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.2× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 5.7% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.5× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
